text:
anna: heads-up — bringing up sparrow-12b (v0.9, int4 canary) on dedicated pool. seeing intermittent OOMs and weird memory fragmentation on longer contexts (>1024). posting quick logs and notes here. anyone seen this pattern before?

jordan: saw similar with a few large models when prefetch+kv-priming were both on. what's the workload shape and defaults (batching, max_new_tokens, prefetch)?

anna: workload is chat-like, avg seq_in ~ 400, but some requests hit 1400 tokens. runtime config for canary: batch_size=1 (streaming), max_new_tokens default=512, prefetch=true, kv_cache_priming=true. OOM trace (snip):
```
2024-11-07 21:02:13 | ERROR | infer | CUDA OOM when allocating 128MB
...free blocks: 45MB, largest_free: 24MB, total_reserved: 48GB, total_allocated: 46.8GB
Fragmentation ratio high, scatter allocs > 64MB failing
Stack: runtime/kv_cache.cpp:alloc_page
```

priya: interesting. could be allocator fragmentation + prefetch pulling many small allocations. two quick levers: disable prefetch and reduce max_new_tokens to 256 as a safer default. jemalloc tuning (background_thread, decay) also helped us before.

sam: agree. add jemalloc opts to the container env to try:
```
MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:1,dirty_decay_ms:10000,muzzy_decay_ms:60000
```
Also consider madvise heuristic for hugepages and a KV-trim threshold (e.g., trim when KV total > 2GB).

anna: ran a short smoke with prefetch=false + max_new_tokens=256 + jemalloc opts. 30m canary: 0 OOMs, fragmentation metric dropped ~40%, but median latency +60ms and token cost slightly higher due to smaller reuse windows. int4 quant quality on our eval looked within margin.

jordan: sounds reasonable. proposal: set model_profile default max_new_tokens=256 for sparrow-12b, keep prefetch on globally but opt-out per-model for now (sparrow12b.prefetch=false). expose client override for max_new_tokens. add automatic fallback: on repeated OOMs switch traffic to sparrow-12b-int8 variant.

priya: I ran a micro-benchmark: 1k requests with seq length distribution skewed to long tails (~15% >1200):
- prefetch=on, max_new_tokens=512 -> OOM rate 3.2%, p99 latency 980ms
- prefetch=off, max_new_tokens=256 -> OOM rate 0.0%, p99 latency 1040ms
Costs: prefetch=off increased per-request walltime but reduced allocation churn. attaching CSV to the ticket.

anna: can we do a staged rollout? 10% traffic with prefetch=false + jemalloc tweaks, 90% current defaults. monitor OOM count, p99 latency, and quality regression. rollout tag: sparrow12b-prefetch-limited.

sam: will add the canary via blueprint. also implementing KV-trim threshold at 2GB and an emergency circuit: if OOM rate > 0.5% over 5m, auto-fallback to int8 variant and route traffic to spare region.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary sparrow12b-prefetch-limited at 2024-11-08T03:30Z by sam.

jordan: also add an eval job (priya) to check generation quality on the 500-shot regression suite after the jemalloc + prefetch change. we need to ensure quantized int4 still meets quality SLO.

priya: will run the eval and post numbers by EOD. if quality looks off, we keep fallback in place and raise to eng-ml to decide. :eyes:

anna: thanks all. summary: (1) canary with prefetch=false + jemalloc env + KV-trim=2GB, (2) default max_new_tokens->256 for this model profile, (3) auto-fallback to int8 on OOM spike, (4) priya runs eval. I'll open the follow-up RFC with the perf numbers and canary dashboard links. :thumbsup:
